messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: RDMA packet-loss spike detected in cluster serving-cluster-3 -> increased latency + cascading CUDA OOMs on multi-node serving groups. Severity: P1. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/rdma-fabric. Pager details -> https://incidents/3101234567
lee (oncall): acknowledged. Jumping in. tagging @taylor @sam @anya. Will take incident lead.
sam (runtime): seeing repeated stack traces from the model pods: `cudaMalloc failed: out of memory` and lots of rdma retransmit errors in dmesg. Happens across 3 nodes in rack-3. Example snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T21:07:02Z] serve: ERROR: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-15T21:07:02Z] ib: RDMA retransmit: order=5, seq=12345, retries=50
[2026-03-15T21:07:03Z] k8s: container crashloop backoff: exit code 137
```
taylor (sre): thanks sam. First things first: isolate traffic from rack-3 to stop cross-node KV cache thrash. Adding node drain and cordon.
Run: 
```bash
kubectl cordon rack-3-node12 -n serving
kubectl drain rack-3-node12 --ignore-daemonsets --timeout=5m -n serving
```
lee (oncall): doing cordon+drain now for node12/13/14. Noting customer impact in thread.
anya (netops): seeing interface flaps on ToR3. Counters: `if_in_errors` and `ib_retransmits` spiked at 21:06:50. Suspect microburst or failing ASIC port. Dump of counters: 
```
ToR3# show interface counters | include err
Gi1/0/12: input-errors=3245, drops=1023, retr=512
Gi1/0/13: input-errors=0, drops=0, retr=0  (peer failover path)
IB-SW# counters retransmits  rack-3: 2450 -> baseline 2
```
anya (netops): I'm pausing RDMA paths to that rack while we triage. Will fail traffic to redundant fabric. Expect some increased latency for affected flows for ~2-5m.
sam (runtime): quick mitigation: reduce batch size and disable KV-prefetch on the model service for requests routed to cluster-3. Applying a runtime flag so OOMs reduce while fabric is degraded.
Command: 
```bash
kubectl set env deploy/gpt-large BATCH_SIZE=1 KV_PREFETCH=false -n serving
```
deploy-bot: deploy started for deploy/gpt-large (image redwood/gpt-large:2026-03-15-hotfix) by sam
deploy-bot: deploy succeeded (revision v2026-03-15-hotfix) :white_check_mark:
lee (oncall): maria (support) please draft an update for affected customers. We have ~12% of requests hitting the degraded rack, error rate peaked at 8%.
maria (support): draft in progress. sending initial customer notification to tenants flagged with routing to cluster-3. Will include mitigation steps and ETA.
anya (netops): replaced ToR3 SFP/module on port 12; counters reset. Monitoring retr/err for 10m. So far packets retransmits down to baseline.
sam (runtime): after draining node12-14 and restarting affected pods, OOMs have subsided. Observed gradual KV cache warmup and token latency returning to SLO.
lee (oncall): handoff: I'll hand to night oncall @jamie in 40m once we've observed stability for 30m. Creating brief runbook notes: cordon/drain nodes, reduce BATCH_SIZE, disable KV_PREFETCH, replace ToR port if counters high, notify customers.
taylor (sre): logging required artifacts: pod logs, dmesg, switch counters, and kvcache hit rate pre/post. Opening tickets for root-cause with netops and runtime teams.
maria (support): customer update sent. No escalations yet; CS will watch for replies.
anya (netops): continuing fabric monitoring. Will keep this channel updated. If we see retransmit > 200 in next 10m, we'll roll traffic away again.
lee (oncall): summary: cause = ToR port microburst/flapping leading to RDMA retransmits -> KV cache thrash -> increased memory pressure -> CUDA OOMs -> container restarts. Mitigations: cordon+drain, reduce batch, disable prefetch, replace ToR module, fail traffic to redundant fabric. Impact: ~12% requests degraded, 8% error spike. Postmortem planned. :thumbsup:
